title_prefix: Orphan intake registers only the deliver
mechanism: Core's orphan branch of MempoolRejectedTx (refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:363-419) does two things ours does not. It erases from the parent list every parent it already has -- std::erase_if(unique_parents, AlreadyHaveTx(txid, include_reconsiderable=false)) at :394-396, where AlreadyHaveTx (:125-148) covers the orphanage, the recently-confirmed filter, the main rejects filter and the mempool. And it enrols more than the delivering peer: orphan_resolution_candidates starts as {nodeid} (:408) and is then extended by GetCandidatePeers over the orphan's txid AND its wtxid (:409-410, implementation at refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:568-576), with MaybeAddOrphanResolutionCandidate plus m_orphanage->AddTx run for EVERY resulting nodeid (:412-415). Only after that does it ForgetTxHash the orphan (:418-419). Ours (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1895-1905) hands request-orphan-parents (:1638-1677) the raw missing-parent-txids list (:1620-1636), filtered against the UTXO set and the mempool only, and passes the delivering peer alone; there is no GetCandidatePeers equivalent anywhere. Two interlocks matter. Our %orphan-parents-rejected-p (:1796-1814) already fails the whole orphan when a parent is in the main rejects filter, and missing-parent-txids already drops parents in the UTXO set or mempool, so the residual filter gap is the ORPHANAGE: a parent we are already holding as an orphan is requested again. And our tracker is wiped before the orphan branch even runs -- handle-tx calls tx-request-received on both ids at :1847-1849, which is ForgetTxHash for ALL peers (the separate S2 dd85e71f) -- so a GetCandidatePeers port would find an empty candidate list until that is fixed. Our only other enrolment path, %maybe-add-orphan-resolution-candidate (:731-753), fires only if such a peer RE-announces the orphan by wtxid afterwards, and it does apply the %already-have-tx-p parent filter the intake path omits.
consequence: Orphan resolution starts with one candidate. Peers that announced the orphan before it reached us -- exactly the ones Core's GetCandidatePeers enrols -- are never registered, and since a peer announces a transaction once, they will not re-announce it, so our %maybe-add-orphan-resolution-candidate fallback never fires for them. If the sole candidate stalls, the parent request dies at the 60 s expiry with no alternative announcer and the orphan waits. The cost is delay, not loss: the missing parent is being relayed normally, so an ordinary inv from any peer still brings it in and re-triggers the orphan, and a peer that announces the orphan LATER still becomes a candidate. The unfiltered parent list adds one redundant full-transaction download per parent we are already holding as an orphan. No transaction is lost and the delay is bounded by ordinary relay, so S3, not the censorship lever GetCandidatePeers exists to blunt in full.
evidence: Probe ga11-txrelay-orphan-intake (scripts/dev.sh load + eval), warm image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, real handlers over the P2SH(OP_TRUE) package fixture (bitcoin-lisp.test-support:make-package-fixture), fresh rejects and recently-confirmed filters, *cached-is-ibd* NIL. (1) Positive control that the send capture is live: (('ctl' 'getdata' 37)). (2) Control, peer A delivers orphan P whose parent U is unknown: (:ORPHAN-STORED T :ORPHAN-ANNOUNCERS-A T :PARENT-U-ANNOUNCERS ('A') :PARENT-U-INFLIGHT NIL) -- intake works and registers A. (3) Peer B (wtxid-relay) announces the CHILD's wtxid before A delivers it: :B-ANNOUNCED-CHILD-BEFORE-DELIVERY ('B'), a live tracker announcement of exactly the kind GetCandidatePeers looks for. After A delivers the child: (:CHILD-STORED T :ORPHANAGE-ANNOUNCER-A T :ORPHANAGE-ANNOUNCER-B NIL :CHILD-WTXID-ANNOUNCERS-AFTER-DELIVERY NIL) -- B is not enrolled anywhere, and its tracker announcement has already been erased by tx-request-received. (4) The parent filter: the child's only missing parent is P, which we hold in the orphanage -- (:PARENT-P-IN-ORPHANAGE T :PARENT-P-ANNOUNCERS ('A') :PARENT-P-INFLIGHT NIL), and once the txid-relay delay is backdated the scheduler sends it: :SCHEDULER-AFTER-DELAY (('A' 'getdata' 37)), a getdata for a transaction we already have. Ours: src/networking/protocol.lisp:1620-1636, :1638-1677, :1796-1814, :1847-1849, :1895-1905, :705-729, :731-753. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:125-148, :363-419; refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:568-576.
fix_shape: Filter the parents, then widen the candidate set, in Core's order. In the :missing-input branch of handle-tx, after %orphan-parents-rejected-p has cleared the orphan, run the parent list through %already-have-tx-p with include-reconsiderable NIL before handing it to request-orphan-parents -- the same call %maybe-add-orphan-resolution-candidate already makes at protocol.lisp:745-748, matching txdownloadman_impl.cpp:394-396; that alone removes the orphanage and recently-confirmed re-requests, and Core's comment explains why reconsiderable must stay excluded (the low-feerate parent is what the child exists to fee-bump). Then add a GetCandidatePeers equivalent to the tracker: a function that returns every peer with a live announcement of a given hash, called for the orphan's txid and, when it has a witness, its wtxid, with the delivering peer at the head; enrol each returned peer through the existing request-orphan-parents plus bl.mp:orphan-add pair so each becomes both a tracker announcer of the parents and an orphanage announcer, as txdownloadman_impl.cpp:408-415 does. That port is inert until the ordering bug it depends on is fixed: handle-tx currently calls tx-request-received (ForgetTxHash, all peers) at :1847-1849 before validation, so the candidate list is already empty by the time the orphan branch runs. Core resolves the delivering peer's announcement only (ReceivedResponse) at receipt and defers ForgetTxHash to :418-419, after the candidates have been collected -- so this finding should be fixed together with, and after, that one.
